metaDescription: Ranch fencing in West, TX built for blackland soil. Barbed wire, pipe fence, game fence and gates for farms off I-35. Free estimates. Call (509) 351-8404.
heroSub: From row-crop ground east of I-35 to cattle places out toward Tokio and Leroy, we build fence that stands up to blackland clay. Free written estimates and a 24/7 line for cattle-out emergencies.
introHtml:
West sits on some of the best blackland prairie in Central Texas, and anybody who farms or runs cattle around here knows what that black gumbo does to a fence. It swells up tight in a wet spring, then cracks open wide in August, and a post that wasn't set right starts leaning by year two. Brazos Ridge Fence Co. builds ranch fencing around West that's planned for that soil from the first hole, with deeper sets and concrete where the ground calls for it.

We're based out of Waco, about 20 minutes down I-35, so getting a crew to your place is easy. We handle barbed wire, pipe fence, game fence, and entrance gates for farms and ranches across northern McLennan County. Every job starts with a free written estimate, priced by the foot so you know the real number before we drive a single post.

services.title: Barbed Wire Fencing
services.desc: Five and six strand barbed wire is still the workhorse on cattle ground around West, and most jobs here run in the $2 to $4 per foot range depending on terrain and corners. We set line posts deep enough to ride out the shrink and swell of blackland clay.

services.title: Pipe Fencing
services.desc: For pens, corrals, and road frontage along FM 2114 or the I-35 access roads, welded pipe fence takes a beating from cattle and weather alike. It costs more up front than wire, but on heavy-use areas it's the last fence you'll build.

services.title: Game Fencing
services.desc: High fence makes sense on larger tracts north and west of town where deer pressure is real. We run 8 foot net wire with braced corners engineered for the long pulls you get on open prairie ground.

services.title: Ranch Entrance Gates
services.desc: A lot of the family places around West have been handed down for generations, and a solid entrance says so. We build pipe entrances and swing gates sized for grain trucks, stock trailers, and cotton strippers turning in off the county road.

sections.heading: Fence Built for Blackland Prairie Ground
sections.html:
The farmland around West is classic blackland prairie, the same heavy clay that grows good cotton, corn, and milo. That soil is hard on fences. It holds water in winter, opens up cracks you can lose a fence pliers in by late summer, and it'll heave a shallow-set post right out of line.

Our fix isn't complicated, it's just doing the work right. We dig corner and gate posts deeper than most, concrete the braces, and stretch wire with the tension the span actually needs. On long straight runs across open crop ground, we add extra bracing so a quarter mile pull stays tight through wet and dry cycles.

We also plan around how you farm. If you're turning equipment at the end rows, we'll set the fence line and gates so a planter or stripper isn't fighting the corners. Little decisions like that are the difference between a fence you like and a fence you curse every season.

sections.heading: Serving West and the Farms Around It
sections.html:
We work all around West, from the edge of town out to the rural routes toward Leroy, Ross, Tours, and Elm Mott, and up toward the Hill County line by Abbott. If your ground touches northern McLennan County, you're in our regular service area, not a maybe.

West's Czech farming families built this area on hard work and land that gets passed down, and we treat every place that way. Whether it's 15 acres with a few head or a full section of row crop with cattle on the back pasture, the estimate is written, the price is per foot, and the crew shows up when we say they will.

We also cover the rest of the county. If you've got family or neighbors with places near China Spring, Crawford, or Valley Mills, we run crews out that way every week.

sections.heading: What Ranch Fencing Costs Around West
sections.html:
Straight talk on numbers: most barbed wire around West lands between $2 and $4 a foot installed. Net wire for goats, sheep, or mixed stock usually runs $3 to $5. Pipe fence for pens and frontage is a bigger investment, often $12 to $25 a foot depending on pipe size and spacing, and high game fence typically falls in the $4 to $8 range.

What moves the price on blackland ground is mostly corners, gates, and old fence removal. Tearing out 70 year old rusted wire with bois d'arc posts takes real time, and every corner brace is money. That's why we walk the line with you before quoting anything. For a fuller breakdown by fence type, see our ranch fence cost guide.

Storm damage is its own deal. When a spring storm rolls up the I-35 corridor and drops a tree across your fence with cattle standing at the gap, call the 24/7 line at (509) 351-8404 and we'll get it patched before your herd finds the highway.

faq.q: Do you build fence on blackland clay around West without the posts heaving?
faq.a: Yes, and it comes down to depth and concrete. Blackland clay swells and shrinks more than almost any soil in Texas, so we set corner and gate posts deeper than standard practice and concrete the load-bearing points. Line posts get driven or set to a depth that keeps them solid through the wet-dry cycle.

faq.q: How much does barbed wire fence cost per foot near West, TX?
faq.a: Most 5 strand barbed wire jobs around West run $2 to $4 per foot installed. Clean, flat crop ground with few corners lands at the low end, while jobs with old fence removal, brush, or lots of gates run higher. We give you a free written estimate with the per-foot price spelled out.

faq.q: Can you fence around active row-crop fields?
faq.a: We do it all the time around West. We'll schedule work between planting and harvest when we can, keep equipment off your beds, and set gates wide enough for combines, grain carts, and cotton strippers. Tell us how you turn at the end rows and we'll plan the line around it.

faq.q: How fast can you get to West for a cattle-out emergency?
faq.a: We're based in Waco, so a crew can usually be on your place in under an hour, day or night. Call the 24/7 emergency line at (509) 351-8404 and we'll get a temporary patch up fast, then come back for the permanent repair. Getting cattle off the road near I-35 can't wait until morning, and we treat it that way.
